The combination of hypopigmented macules, eyebrow thinning, and loss of eyelashes alongside neuropathic symptoms is highly suggestive of Hansen's disease. I will request a slit-skin smear to confirm the presence of acid-fast bacilli.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal slit-skin smear makes Hansen's disease less likely, so I need to explore other causes for your neuropathy and rash. Have you experienced any recent weight loss, fever, or night sweats, and do you have a history of diabetes or alcohol use?

speaker: Doctor
text:
The patient's presentation of hypopigmented macules, madarosis (loss of eyebrows/eyelashes), and peripheral neuropathy is classic for leprosy, even with a negative initial slit-skin smear. I will request a skin biopsy to look for granulomas and acid-fast bacilli to confirm the diagnosis.
